title: I had high hopes for this product after judging reviews and cost.
text:
Im actually sad about this product because I had high hopes for it, considering they’d been open since 1978, used natural products and their production process was so different than most , i.e. no dipping, use bamboo wood, etc., the whole thing just seemed promising to me.

Now, I can tell there is pride in their product because it doesn’t seem cheaply made and even the box is made of a nice, sturdy material but the aroma it gave off was quite horrid. I’m not sure if maybe they put the wrong type in the box, because the outside does say lavender but, this literally smells like a forest fire.

Funny thing was, after I lit one, my brother came into the room and just straight up asked me what caught fire. A few minutes later my buddy walked in and just started frantically waving his hands saying he wouldn’t even step foot in my room.

Later on I gave one to my mom to get her opinion and when I care back a few minutes later to ask her, I found it faced down in her plant, extinguished (that’s what my pic is of. Lol I thought that was funny).

I’m sending it back because $17 for a product I’m never using again is just a waste in my mind. So, I’m hoping to take advantage of their money back guarantee. I only took out two.

Actually, they even inserted and extra envelope with about 6 different additional sent samples but I’m not even going to open that. I’ll return it with the rest of the bunch to better ensure getting my money back. I wasn’t trying to play them. I REALLY wanted it to smell nice. I would’ve even gone for “decent”... passable.

I will say, AFTER it completely died out and a while passed (half hour), there was a SLIGHT lingering floral sent in the air; minuscule. That’s the reason I won’t give just one star... that and the packaging/obvious pride in their product. Again, maybe I just got a faulty pack but, I’m not willing to gamble it again.

Last night I was making an enchilada sauce, and while the pan was over medium heat I very slowly poured in 2 cups of chicken stock that I had taken out of the fridge.... this I would later discover had warped the pan just slightly (this was one of the first dishes I'd made with the new pan).

While the replacement pan is by no means totally ruined, it is incredibly frustrating that it is so seemingly delicate that it would warp, right out of the box, from one instance of very normal usage. I'm not sure if this is just the nature of tri-ply stainless steel, or if this would perhaps not have happened with a more expensive All Clad pan. From now on I will make sure to heat any liquids I include into the pan in the microwave beforehand to hopefully prevent any further warping.

My mother is Christian and my father is Jewish but they both celebrate Christmas. I wish I could say good things about this cool interfaith star but it has three fatal flaws:

1. The metal is thin enough that it is easily bent. Indeed, one of the corners of the Star was slightly bent upon arrival but was easily bent back into shape.

It also this means that the tree only looks good if viewed directly from the front. Everyone who sees it from the side or back will have an unsightly view of the 'hardware' on the back where the star attaches to the tree.

Good idea in concept but flawed in its execution in several ways that were avoidable. Too bad.

I bought it not to use for shoes but as a side table for my TV recliner to hold everything from a lamp, phone, and laptop computer with case to a half dozen or so remote controls and a Family Size box of Cheez-It crackers. I spent over an hour trying everything I could think of to make that nut and bolt pair merge. I took a break for dinner and tried some more. No deal. In the end, it looks like I stripped the threads on the end of the bolt, and maybe it can no longer get started properly in the nut. But it doesn’t really matter. The loose bolt does not show where I have the table placed and the table is plenty strong without it.

I highly recommend this bench/table. Just don’t let it ruin your dinner.

title: Not a Bad Fan
text:
I've had this tower fan for over a year and it has performed about as well as I expected. Its not as quiet as I would like, but why ask for the impossible? It's a fan and it's going go make a bit fan noise while its on. Mostly it fades into the background. It blows well (that's what fans do) and oscillates which seems to efficiently circulate the air in my small bedroom/apartment and makes a big difference on hot days -- no central AC, here. I really like the remote and built in nook for it on the top of the fan. It's nice not having to get out of bed to adjust the settings in the middle of the night.

I don't like that the lighted display can't be dimmed or turned off. The light is very very bright in a dark room. I usually put a ball-cap over the top of the fan at night so it doesn't glare at me while I'm sleeping like an air-circulating eye of Sauron. Also, the "nature" setting, which I assume is supposed to mimic the ebb and flow of natural wind outside, is probably the most annoying thing I've ever experienced a fan do in my life as it constantly changes speed and cuts out into still, dead silence at intervals -- try sleeping with it on that setting. Dare ya.

Overall worth the money, I suppose.

title: Good for upholstery, not the best for carpeted stairs
text:
This little vacuum works fairly well for upholstery and the cord is very long so you don't have to move the plug constantly. However, I had hoped it would do a better job on our carpeted stairs. Note there is no rotating brush--this vacuum couples suction with a rubber tip for gathering up hair. It does work, but it can be tedious when you have to cover the same patch of carpet several times to really get the hair up, as is often the case. The "power paw" vacuum hose attachments do seem to work better, but every one I've tried quit working within a few months. Here are some pros and cons to consider for carpeted stairs:
Pet Hair Eraser
Pros: light weight, long cord
Cons: often requires multiple passes (slow), need to empty out hair frequently
Power Paw (hose attachment)
Pros: works very well, emptying infrequent
Cons: really noisy, not durable, requires you to lug the vacuum up every few steps
Regular Vacuum
Pros: works better and faster than the other options, quieter, emptying infrequent
Cons: it's really awkward and heavy to vacuum stairs

Note that none of the three does a good job getting into the corners of the steps--the vacuum hose is still the best bet there, although the crevice tool attachment for the pet hair eraser works reasonably well if you also ball up any matter hair with your fingers.

title: So firm it hurts, caused jaw pain
text:
This thing is just painfully firm. I bought it to use when I got a helix piercing (I sleep with my left ear in the hole on one side every night and my right ear just on a regular pillow when I roll.) While the discomfort has helped me a lot with not sleeping on my piercing at all since it disrupts my sleep so much, I’ve not gotten a decent night’s sleep in 2 months. I strongly recommend buying it if you want to train yourself to not roll in your sleep with physical pain if you do roll. I’ve gone from moving a lot in my sleep to being stiff as a board from the threat of having to sleep on this thing.

As a travel pillow, it sucks. I don’t even use it anymore to travel when I have no other options. Literally just letting your head dangle with no support hurts less. I can’t imagine any hard surface being less comfortable.

Additionally, this pillow has severely increased my jaw pain on the side I sleep on it. It hurts even when I use it as intended with my neck in the pillow. Honestly, I think even if you don’t have a history of TMJ, using this thing daily could certainly give you that history of TMJ. Say goodbye to eating large burgers or sandwiches if you use this regularly.

The microfiber cover is soft to the touch, but you cannot remove it to wash since it’s just stuffed with loose, hair-like fibers. Idk how to go about washing this thing.

Tldr; get any other travel pillow unless you like pain.

title: Great Product
text:
I don't normally give 5 stars to anything but this product deserves it with one minor exepction below. I give it a 4 stars since there is not a 4.5 stars option.
We have owned it for 15 months and have had no real problems with it at all.
With the clear dirt container is easy to see when it needs emptying. The suction is quite adequate and the power head works well. We use it on both hardwood floors and large area rugs. It is easy to pull around. The telescoping wand is a good feature. A concern before the purchase was the effectiveness and durability of the cord retractor. Much to my delight it continues to work well with no problems. The filter is easy to remove, clean and replace.
The hard surface head has a bit of a funky fit to the wand but there has been no probem with it coming off. It did cause an initial concern. The locking pin for the power head gets pushed in when the hard surface head is attached. Because of this, pet hair got caught under the holding spring for the pin; keeping it from extending all the way out when the power head was attached. This caused the power head to come off when the wand was pulled toward you. At first I thought it was defective but just before I called Hoover to complain I noticed the hair trapped under the spring. Upon removing the hair the pin extended all the way and the power head stayed on the wand with no further issues.
I definitely recommend this product.

2016-12-10
Still works as well as when we bought it in 2009. Bought a replacement filter to have one in while we washed the old one. Switch out when filter needs cleaning again. Cord still retracts as well as when it was new. Definitely a great product.

title: 9 mths later...
text:
I bought this to keep beverages chilled on my desk at work, and so far have liked it. It has done a really nice job of keeping beverages cool throughout an 8-hour workday. It can even reasonably cool a beverage in a pinch, especially if that beverage is in a metal container. Just put the beverage in the holder, roll your finger over the touch-sensitive on/off button on the side, and the cooler turns on and does its thing.

HOWEVER, here comes the iffy part of this purchase. It has been 9 months since I purchased this item, and it is showing signs of wear. Now when I turn on the device, it has started making a loud screeching noise as if the fan is wearing out. So far, turning it off and on again takes care of the problem, but it makes me wonder if the item was not made for use 5 days a week, 8 hours a day, which is what I bought it for.

So keep that in mind when looking at this item for purchase. Do you intend to use it as I do throughout the work day/week, or will you use it only part of the time? Based on the noise it has begun making after 9 months of ownership, I assume that the cooler is not made for long-term heavy every day use. I will be interested to see how much longer it holds out. Otherwise, it's been a nice little desktop beverage cooler.

title: Keeps the humidity in my basement full of plants to an acceptable level.
text:
We have a large basement with 3 rooms that I grow a number of vegetables and herbs in. Prior to getting this dehumidifier, the humidity in our basement was continuously in excess of 70% caused by evaporation of water in the pots. Unfortunately, we were told this caused humidity in our attic that wasn't noticed until we found mold growing. This was a very expensive lesson for us as we had to have the roof and all of the wood below it replaced at a cost of over $15K.

I am not going to get into any technical stuff like the efficiency of the condenser, but will say this dehumidifier has helped to solve our humidity problem. In searching for a dehumidifier to meet our needs, I had to learn the capacity of humidity remove was different than the size of the tank to be emptied. The 50 pint ( or 6.25 gallons) capacity of this dehumidifier is the amount of moisture that will be removed from the air in a 24 hour period. I would guess the water tank holds about 2 gallons of water as we need to empty it 3 times in a 24 hour period.

Since the humidity in our basement is high because of the plants, we have this unit set to continuous, but you can also set it to run until a desired humidity is reached. When the water container is full, it automatically stops until the container is emptied. You can also set the fan to high or low. When the filter gets dirty, a light shows on the top of the unit. Cleaning the filter is a matter of spraying it clean with a faucet spray and drying it with a towel.

This unit is in a room 30' x 15', and the humidity has been reduced from over 70% to 40%. We have had this dehumidifier for over a month, and are very happy with it. It consistently keeps the humidity down and is very easy to maintain.

UPDATE 5/27/22:
Since our basement is very large with 3 rooms, two of which contain plants, we decided to buy another one of these dehumidifiers so we could one in each of the plant rooms. The humidity in both rooms is staying around 40% and out attic is now staying dry. This has also helped to reduce the humidity in the house which make it much more comfortable during the summer.

I hope this review was helpful for you.

title: LOVE this oven
text:
I absolutely love this model (Smart Oven Air) from the moment I saw it. Everything I was looking for. But, initially, I was shocked at the thought of spending so much on a countertop oven. So I researched for weeks online and in stores trying to find something more affordable with the features I wanted. I narrowed it down and settled on a cheaper model (Nuwave Bravo 30qt) - which turned out to be crap quality so I returned it and decided this is the one I needed and should have not wasted my time on the other one.

This one blows them all out of the water with it's quality, size and so many features, including dehydrate. The control panel being off to the side with a cooling fan that stays on after the oven shuts off is a big plus too. I also like that there is enough space for a full size frozen pizza because of the way the backside has a rounded part that extends out past the rest of the regular cube shape.

Living in AZ, I am really looking forward to using this outside in my covered patio when the weather gets hot - no need to fire up the regular oven and have the AC work even harder. That alone justifies the price for me! Regardless of where you live, this is a really nice oven with the size and features to handle nearly anything.

p.s. if you want the extra air fry mesh trays, get them at Williams Sonoma (Breville Smart Oven Air Mesh Baskets, Set of 3)
